results.title: The billion-dollar remote work opportunity that rural America can’t reach | Fortune
results.content: # The billion-dollar remote work opportunity that rural America can’t reach. The U.S. has spent billions to bring broadband to rural communities—but many of the people it’s meant to help still aren’t logging on. Unless governments focus on adoption—not just access—they risk funding infrastructure that goes unused, while rural Americans remain cut off from healthcare, education,and the growing remote job market that today represents nearly a quarter of the U.S. workforce. Most public discussion around rural broadband has centered on availability. Across rural America, broadband networks are expanding—yet adoption remains stubbornly low in many regions. As recently as 2021, nearly one in five rural households did not subscribe to a broadband service. By 2023, broadband adoption had surpassed 80% among younger rural adults, but dropped sharply with age. Just 68% of rural adults over 75 had broadband. Even in communities where broadband is already available, uptake lags for reasons that go beyond infrastructure or cost. A study of broadband deployment in rural Missouri found that most early adopters used their new connection primarily for entertainment. Counties with high broadband adoption see stronger job growth, higher self-employment, and greater income gains.Nationally, about 22% of the workforce—roughly 32 million Americans—now works remotely at least part of the time, compared to just 6% before the pandemic. While the Covid-era boom in remote or hybrid work has cooled, the share of remote-capable jobs remains an enduring opportunity for rural communities positioned to take advantage of it. But while three-quarters of mid-career rural workers say they’re willing to train for those jobs, most say they haven’t taken any courses to do so — often because they lack the broadband access to even start. In Ohio and West Virginia, providers report low digital adoption among seniors despite widespread broadband availability. Solving the broadband adoption gap must begin at the local level. These places and resources serve as anchors in many rural communities and are well positioned to explain how broadband supports everyday needs. Some states have created digital navigator programs that train local leaders to help residents use the internet with confidence.

results.title: Participant recruitment strategies in research – Dr Lynette Pretorius
results.content: Instead of engaging in time-consuming and resource-intensive processes to identify and recruit participants, convenience sampling allows researchers to gather data from those who happen to be in the right place at the right time, or who meet the study’s basic criteria and are easy to contact. In purposive sampling, researchers carefully define the criteria for inclusion, selecting participants based on how well they fit the study’s needs. In studies involving niche groups, such as people with rare medical conditions or members of specific subcultures, purposive sampling enables researchers to focus on finding individuals who meet the study’s strict criteria, bypassing the need for broader recruitment efforts that may yield less relevant participants. If the research is designed to draw conclusions about the broader population, such as in public health research, market research, or large-scale sociological studies, random sampling is ideal because it provides the most unbiased and representative data possible. Stratified sampling is a method used by researchers to ensure that their sample accurately reflects the diversity of the population by focusing on key subgroups, or “strata.” The basic idea is that the population is divided into distinct groups based on important characteristics such as age, gender, income level, education, or ethnicity. Moreover, by dividing the population into strata and then randomly selecting participants from each group, stratified sampling ensures a more balanced and accurate representation, which minimises the risk of sampling errors. While stratified sampling relies on random selection from each subgroup, quota sampling allows researchers to directly control who is recruited by actively seeking participants to fill predefined quotas based on certain characteristics, such as age, gender, education level, or income. Since the researcher can directly seek out participants who meet the required criteria, the process can be completed more quickly and at a lower cost than methods like stratified sampling. Since participants are not selected randomly, there is a risk that the sample may not accurately represent the broader population, even if the quotas are met. For example, in research involving focus groups or interviews, where the goal is to gather in-depth insights from specific subgroups, quota sampling allows the researcher to select participants who fit the desired profile without the logistical complexities of random selection.

results.title: Recruitment CRM Strategies for Effectively Engaging Candidates
results.content: Automation lies at the heart of effective candidate engagement, and recruitment CRM platforms excel in automating communication workflows to ensure timely and relevant interactions with candidates. Recruitment CRM platforms offer seamless integration with a diverse range of communication channels, enabling recruiters to engage candidates wherever they are most active. Whether it’s sending personalized emails, connecting via LinkedIn messages, or engaging in real-time chats, CRM-integrated communication channels ensure that recruiters can reach candidates effectively and foster meaningful interactions. Recruitment CRM platforms leverage advanced integration capabilities to synchronize communication across different channels, providing recruiters with a unified view of candidate interactions and engagement metrics. By centralizing communication data within CRM systems, recruiters can track candidate engagement across various touchpoints, measure the effectiveness of different communication channels, and gain actionable insights to optimize engagement strategies. Moreover, recruitment CRM platforms facilitate personalized communication experiences across all channels, ensuring that candidates receive relevant and timely messages that resonate with their preferences and interests.
